correctness.rationale: Transport the quandle product to the ordinary commutative group ring B=R[G] as u⋆v=α(u)β(v), where α(X^g)=X^{Tg}, β(X^g)=X^{(1-T)g}; direct expansion yields [u,v,w]=αβ(v)(α²(u)β(w)-α(u)β²(w)). Each basis associator is an H=(1-T)G difference. The particular associator [e_x,e_x,e_{x+d}] gives e_{x+(1-T)d}-e_{x+(1-T)²d}, whose shift T(1-T)d ranges over H; translating x realizes all subgroup differences. Thus the entire R-span equals ker(R[G]→R[G/H]), which is a ⋆-ideal because the quotient has left-zero multiplication. For Latin β, the augmentation ideal I has annihilator RΩ by coefficient shift equalities independent of zero divisors. Substituting 1_B into the associator in all three placements forces each nucleus into RΩ, while Ω⋆x=x⋆Ω=ε(x)Ω proves the converse, Ω²=|G|Ω. Verified independent cyclic small-case structure and original checker source, not treating finite tests as universal proof.
residual_risks: The general three-nucleus formula assumes both T and 1-T invertible; no non-Latin nucleus classification.
The modular square-zero identity concerns Ω, not whole algebra; no division by |G| was used.
